title: Wedding Reception Games for Guests: 30 Ideas + What to Skip
description: 30 wedding reception games for guests, sorted by when they fit in the night, each with setup time, cost and a tip, plus a sample timeline and what to skip.
dek: Cocktail hour to last dance: what to play, how long it takes to set up and what to skip.
excerpt: Thirty reception games and activities sorted by cocktail hour, dinner, after the toasts and late night, each with setup time, rough cost and a tip, plus a sample timeline.
secondary_keywords: wedding reception games for bride and groom

faq.q: What are good wedding reception games for guests who don’t know each other?
faq.a: Pick games that give strangers a reason to talk without putting anyone on the spot. Guest bingo built from RSVP facts, team table trivia between courses and a two-truths-and-a-lie sign about the couple all work well. Self-serve activities such as a map of where everyone traveled from or a jigsaw of the couple’s photo let quieter guests join in at their own pace.

faq.q: How many games should you have at a wedding reception?
faq.a: Two or three hosted games, such as the shoe game and an anniversary dance, plus two or three self-serve activities like lawn games, advice cards or a photo scavenger hunt. Keep each hosted game under ten minutes so the timeline holds. Any more than that and the reception starts to feel like a game show instead of a party.

faq.q: When should you play games at a wedding reception?
faq.a: Use the natural gaps. Self-serve games fit cocktail hour, table games fit between dinner courses, and couple games like the shoe game or an anniversary dance fit right after the toasts, just before the dancing opens. Keep games out of the ceremony and the first dance, and save prize announcements for the end of the night or the next morning.

faq.q: What are the best wedding reception games for the bride and groom?
faq.a: The shoe game is the classic: the couple sits back to back and raises a shoe to answer questions about each other. A newlywed quiz built from questions guests submit at dinner, and an anniversary dance that ends with the longest-together couple sharing advice, also put the couple at the center without embarrassing anyone. All three work for any couple.

faq.q: What wedding reception games work indoors?
faq.a: Most of them. Table trivia, love-story mad libs, table poems, name that tune, a jigsaw puzzle, a card table and freeze dance all work in a ballroom or a restaurant. A giant tumbling-block tower fits indoors if your venue allows it, and ribbon limbo needs nothing more than a clear patch of dance floor.
